name: AI-Data Driven Question Blueprint
purpose: Define stable semantic metadata for Lecture-grounded question generation and persistent de-duplication.
runtimePolicy: GitHub Pages does not call an external AI model. AI analyzes Lecture data during automation/build time and writes structured question blueprints for the shared runtime engine.

requiredQuestionMetadata.semanticId: Stable ID for one distinct learning objective or case. Rewording, option shuffling, answer ordering, or equivalent framing must keep the same semanticId.
requiredQuestionMetadata.conceptIds: Stable IDs for Lecture-grounded concepts/relations used by the question.
requiredQuestionMetadata.sourceRefs: Lecture file references that directly support the question, answer, distractors, and explanation.

optionalMetadata.difficultyReason: Why the blueprint belongs to Easy/Medium/Hard at university level.
optionalMetadata.blueprintType: definition | relation | comparison | interpretation | application | case | exception | decision
optionalMetadata.semanticFingerprint: Normalized summary used by AI to detect near-duplicate blueprints.

dedupeRules: Never create a new semanticId only because wording changes.
Never create a new semanticId only because choice order or matching order changes.
Merge near-duplicate blueprints that test the same learning objective with equivalent evidence.
Prefer a new blueprint only when it tests a materially different Lecture-supported relation, condition, interpretation, application, case, exception, or decision.
Question id/serial/option order must never be used as proof that a question is semantically new.
Native and runtime-generated questions that test the same Lecture relation or learning objective must resolve to the same semantic identity whenever derivable.
runtimeDedupeRules: Persist used semantic signatures across refreshes, tabs, and browser sessions using persistent browser storage when available; session-only storage is insufficient.
Mark a semantic signature as used as soon as the question is displayed, not only after the user submits an answer.
Track used semantic signatures by course+mode+level and maintain recent concept history by course.

If semanticId is missing in legacy data, derive a conservative content-based semantic fingerprint from normalized prompt, correct answer/relation, and Lecture-grounded structure; do not fall back to q.id as the primary semantic identity.

When no unseen semantic blueprint remains, stop and report that no new non-duplicate blueprint is available. Do not recycle, reword, reorder, or reshuffle an old semantic question to simulate endlessness.
qualityRules: All facts, answers, distractors, and explanations must be supported by Lecture.
Easy, Medium, and Hard must remain university-level.
Wrong-answer explanations must state why the submitted answer is wrong using Lecture evidence.
If Lecture cannot support another semantically distinct blueprint, do not invent new facts merely to preserve endless flow.
